subject: Defininig different set of colors for different variable class

messages.author: 41efa4e9ec79a6ec
messages.subject: Defininig different set of colors for different variable class
parts:
I want to plot my dataset with 4 different class of variables.
When I use the command below, I get all the plots, but  the coloring of the lines seems random. Anyone knows how to allocate color (or range) for different classes on the same dataframe?

Here is the command which I have been using:

ggplot(data = df.919, aes(x = Depth, y = value, colour = variable)) + geom_line()


Alternatively, I have tried splitting the dataframe (using split function) based on class and then plot the individual dataframes - but ran into problems plotting using the splitlist.

However, even if I succeed with splitting,  Is it possible to have multiple ggplots (geom_lines) on the same plot. It is important for my data presentation to put them on the same plot.

messages.author: 48ac9e0ac86209c2
messages.subject: Re: Defininig different set of colors for different variable class
parts:
Your question is not entirely clear ( "the coloring of the lines seems random"), but I think you are asking if you can pick your own colors for your plot as opposed to the default ones. The below assumes you want to pick your own colors for your four factor levels.


ggplot(data = df.919, aes(x = Depth, y = value, colour = variable)) + geom_line()+
scale_color_manual(values=c("red", "blue", "purple", "red"))

Aksel
